blocking.problem:
PT5 says add/sub of pointer atoms "shifts each pointer atom's offset by each constant (classes and * stay)". This still uses unbounded object-offset arithmetic rather than the integer operation's finite width. PT6 reads represented object intervals without explicitly propagating the address value's non-handle top alternative to the loaded value. Witness:

target datalayout = "e-p:64:64"
@tab = internal constant [1 x ptr] [ptr @body]
declare void @__bennett_adj(ptr, ptr, ptr)
define internal void @body(ptr %e) {
  ret void
}
define void @top() {
  %a = ptrtoint ptr @tab to i64
  %b = add i64 %a, -9223372036854775808
  %c = add i64 %b, -9223372036854775808
  %p = inttoptr i64 %c to ptr
  %f = load ptr, ptr %p, align 8
  call void @__bennett_adj(ptr %f, ptr null, ptr null)
  ret void
}

The unflagged i64 additions have total displacement -2^64, hence zero modulo 2^64: %p equals @tab, %f equals @body, and adj succeeds. No intermediate address is dereferenced; no poison or out-of-bounds access occurs. LLVM 18 and 23 verify and retain this module through default<O0>; instcombine folds the marker operand to ptr nonnull @body on both. The repository recogniser instead returns accept with %b=(tab,9223372036854775808)+TOP, %c/%p=(tab,18446744073709551616)+TOP, %f=empty and candidates=empty. §7.2 then requires T-REGION/code 4, contradicting §18.1’s materialised integer execution. Signed mathematical offset accumulation gives -2^64, equally wrong. Independent lli marker harnesses under host-default layouts call body exactly once on both LLVM 18 and 23 (exit 0). LLVM 23 lli refuses the abbreviated explicit DataLayout, so that direct JIT form is not claimed executed; opt verifies/folds the explicit-layout source on both. This is a new integer-arithmetic/unknown-load hole adjacent to the resolved PT2 finding, not a PT2 regression.
blocking.fix: In §5.2 replace PT5’s pointer-arithmetic clauses with: "For add/sub on an iW value carrying pointer atoms, evaluate address bits modulo 2^W, never by unbounded mathematical displacement. When W equals the source pointer representation width, retain each original object provenance and accumulate relative offsets modulo 2^W; zero net displacement represents the original address. For residue classes and * take the image of all represented addresses and operand values under the same finite-width operation. If the image can leave its represented object, or cannot be represented precisely, additionally include (EXT,*) and the non-handle top flag. For other integer operations on pointer atoms, retain (X,*) for each original X and additionally include (EXT,*) and the non-handle top flag unless an explicitly specified transfer computes a sound image. Handle-derived uses remain governed by §6.2." In PT6 add: "An address operand with the non-handle top flag denotes unknown possible addresses in addition to its explicit atoms. A load through this alternative contributes the non-handle top flag to its loaded value; never drop that alternative because explicit object offsets overlap no known slot. ROOT provenance remains explicit." Apply these rules also to constant expressions and before candidate/dispatch domains freeze. Retain the rest of PT5, including the removed-range rule. Add the witness to DB/DS with verdict accept, RR(%f)={body}, exactly one successful body invocation and no code 4 under adequate budgets, in both O0 and instcombine forms. AV(%f) may conservatively contain TOP but must represent FN(body). Include a non-identity transformation that can reach another allocation, to test unknown-address propagation. A uniformly conservative TOP transfer for pointer-bearing arithmetic is another sound repair if its fixed reference precision/verdict consequences are specified; I recommend the modular provenance-preserving transfer above. No new rejection or ISA change is needed.
